messages:
oliver: Quick pulse check — I reran the batch formation sweep this morning and the numbers look odd. p99 latency on A100 climbed ~12% after the kernel-selector v2 rollout. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: saw that on dashboards, noticed KV hitrate dropped on a10/a100 mix racks around the same time. Could be kv-frag.

sophia: left a quick profile link: https://perf.redwood/internal/2026/kv-frag/sweep-171619 — flamegraphs + shortcall trace. small-batch churn seems to increase kernel fallback.

arjun: short summary of my runs:
- baseline (kernel-v1) -> A100 p99 85ms
- kernel-v2 -> A100 p99 95ms (+12%)
- kernel-v2 + tightened batch token ceiling -> p99 88ms
so kernel-v2 alone not entire cause; interaction with batch-token ceilings and kv fragmentation matters.

oliver: what ceilings did you tighten? numbers?

arjun: per-gpu max_tokens_per_batch used in the test: T4: 12000, L4: 28000, A10: 48000, A100: 96000, H100: 120000. also nudged slice formation to prefer same-seqlen packing.

maya: the actuator that helped was reducing mixed-card packing for A100-heavy slices. mixed packing triggered KV invalidations and forced fallback to memcpy-heavy path on kernel-v2.

sophia: flamegraphs show lots of memcpy + spin waits in kernel-v2 path when KV fragments > ~18k entries — matches the larger mixed batches.

perf-bot: perf alert: job batch-sweep-171619 completed. throughput delta (kernel-v2 vs baseline): -3% overall, p50 unchanged, p99 increased on A100/A10 mix racks. report: s3://redwood-perf/reports/171619-summary.html

oliver: proposed mitigations: 1) per-card soft ceiling (prefer smaller token budgets when mixed-packing detected), 2) queue policy: hold mixed candidate up to 10ms to find seq-length peers, else release, 3) lightweight KV-frag probe to route mixed batches earlier to kernel-v1 fallback. objections?

maya: +1. holding 10ms looks fine for most requests (our p99 SLA ~200ms). need an escape for ultra-low-latency tiny requests.

arjun: implemented (1) and (2) in a dev patch. pseudo-config: ``` batching: max_tokens_per_gpu: T4: 12000 L4: 28000 A10: 48000 A100: 96000 H100: 120000 mixed_pack_hold_ms: 10 mixed_pack_soft_penalty: 0.15 kv: frag_warn_threshold: 18000 route_to_kernel_v1_if_frag: true ```

sophia: ran short A/B on dev cluster (a10+a100 mix) — dev results: kv hitrate +4%, p99 A100 95ms -> 89ms, throughput +1.8%. running extended stability tonight.

infra-bot: deployment scheduled to canary pool_rack_7 at 2026-05-21T09:10:00Z. CI: all green. logs: https://logs.redwood/canary/171619

oliver: regression still unexplained in some A100-only racks. Sophia, can you post seq-length histogram for those racks?

sophia: uploaded histograms to the perf link. A100-only racks show a heavy tail at 40-60k tokens from internal eval runs. that tail spikes KV frag and hits the memcpy fallback. options: eviction-friendly KV layout, prealloc path for >50k sequences, or explicitly route large single-seq requests to kernel-v1 path.

maya: operational note: for Dedicated customers avoid config flips without rollout window. gate soft-ceilings per customer tier.

arjun: will add prefer_strict_ceiling_for_enterprise flag (false by default) and a rollback trigger if p99 >5% for any dedicated pool.

oliver: action items: arjun open PR with config + mixed-pack hold (w/ tests) — EOD; sophia run 24h stability + seq-hists; maya prepare customer-tier rollout notes + monitoring triggers; infra schedule canary + rollback playbook. also add KV-frag probe in request path to increment a metric when fragmentation > frag_warn_threshold to build dataset for selector tuning.

arjun: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821

sophia: preliminary overnight looks promising :thumbsup: will post follow-up after stability run.

perf-bot: nightly job scheduled: batch-sweep-171619-stability at 2026-05-21T03:00:00Z

oliver: if overnight is clean we'll roll canary tomorrow morning. thanks all.
